edits.before: <para id="eip-id1546958"><emphasis effect="bold">3. </emphasis>Neutrino masses may be zero. Experimental upper limits are given in parentheses.</para>
edits.after:
<para id="eip-id1546958"><emphasis effect="bold">3. </emphasis>Neutrino flavors are mixtures of mass states. The entries are direct experimental upper bounds, not measured masses: the electron-based bound is 0.45 eV/c² (KATRIN, 2025; 90% confidence), the muon-based bound is 0.19 MeV/c² (90% confidence), and the tau-based bound is 18.2 MeV/c² (95% confidence). All three entries use the column unit MeV/c². The electron-based measurement constrains an effective mass through tritium beta decay, which emits an electron antineutrino. The weaker muon- and tau-based bounds do not imply that those flavors are heavier.</para>
<para id="neutrino-oscillation-mass-note">Oscillation measurements determine differences between squared masses, with characteristic magnitudes of about <m:math><m:mrow><m:mn>7.5</m:mn><m:mo>×</m:mo><m:msup><m:mn>10</m:mn><m:mrow><m:mo>−</m:mo><m:mn>5</m:mn></m:mrow></m:msup></m:mrow></m:math> and <m:math><m:mrow><m:mn>2.5</m:mn><m:mo>×</m:mo><m:msup><m:mn>10</m:mn><m:mrow><m:mo>−</m:mo><m:mn>3</m:mn></m:mrow></m:msup></m:mrow></m:math> eV²/c⁴. These establish that at least two mass states have nonzero mass, but do not determine the absolute masses. Combined with the electron-based direct bound, oscillation measurements constrain all three mass states.</para>
